### BioMed-Scribe

**Medical Specialty Classification from Clinical Conversations**

::: badges
[Python]{.badge} [GPT-2]{.badge} [NLP]{.badge} [Gradio]{.badge}
:::

Fine-tuned GPT-2 Medium on 13,492 clinical conversations using a two-block parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy.

**Highlights**

- 79.1% test accuracy
- 0.799 macro-F1
- 25.2M trainable parameters
- Four medical specialties
- t-SNE embedding analysis
- Interactive Gradio deployment

::: project-links

:::

### County-Level Lung Cancer Mortality

**Spatial Statistics, Machine Learning, and Public Health**

::: badges
[R]{.badge} [Spatial Statistics]{.badge} [XGBoost]{.badge} [SHAP]{.badge}
:::

Analyzed lung cancer mortality across 2,536 U.S. counties using CDC Social Vulnerability Index, CDC PLACES, and National Cancer Institute data.

**Methods**

- Robust OLS
- Quantile regression
- Moran's I
- LISA
- Spatial error models
- Random Forest
- XGBoost
- SHAP
- Mediation analysis

**Key Results**

- 232 unexplained high-mortality spatial clusters identified
- COPD mediated approximately 50.8% of the county-level smoking–mortality association

::: project-links
[View Report](files/reports/Lung_Cancer_Report.pdf){.btn .btn-sm .btn-primary target="_blank"}
:::
:::::

::::: project-card
### Food Insecurity and Chronic Disease Burden

**County-Level Public Health Analysis**

::: badges
[R]{.badge} [Spatial Analysis]{.badge} [Regression]{.badge} [Mapping]{.badge}
:::

Analyzed 2,299 U.S. counties to examine the relationship between food insecurity and chronic disease burden.

**Methods**

- Standardized chronic disease burden index
- Multivariable regression
- Sensitivity analysis
- Spatial autocorrelation
- Geographic mapping

**Key Results**

- Identified 408 counties with jointly high food insecurity and chronic disease burden
- Significant spatial clustering was observed across the United States

::: project-links
[View Report](files/reports/Food_Insecurity_Chronic_Disease_Burden.pdf){.btn .btn-sm .btn-primary target="_blank"}
:::

::::: project-card
### Cardiovascular Disease Risk Factors

**Gender-Based Comparative Statistical Analysis**

::: badges
[Minitab]{.badge} [Logistic Regression]{.badge} [ROC Analysis]{.badge} [Public Health]{.badge}
:::

Analyzed cardiovascular disease risk factors in a public dataset of 68,672 adults, with emphasis on whether associations differed between women and men.

**Methods**

- Spearman correlation
- Welch's two-sample t test
- Kruskal-Wallis tests
- Chi-square test of independence
- Binary logistic regression
- Gender-specific models
- ROC and AUC analysis

**Key Results**

- Combined logistic model achieved an AUC of approximately 0.791
- Age, BMI, blood pressure, and cholesterol were important predictors of cardiovascular disease
- Gender-specific models showed similar overall risk structures with differences in coefficient magnitude

::: project-links
[View Report](files/reports/Cardiovascular_Disease_Risk_Factors.pdf){.btn .btn-sm .btn-primary target="_blank"}
:::
:::::

### Statistical Analysis of Diabetes Risk Factors

**CDC BRFSS Analysis**

::: badges
[SAS]{.badge} [R]{.badge} [Regression]{.badge} [ANOVA]{.badge}
:::

Analyzed 253,680 CDC BRFSS observations to investigate clinical, behavioral, demographic, and socioeconomic factors associated with diabetes-related outcomes.

**Methods**

- Chi-square tests
- Factorial ANOVA
- Multiple regression
- Logistic regression
- Model selection
- Diagnostics
- Sex-stratified analysis

### Modeling Life Expectancy in Africa

**Socioeconomic and Health Indicators**

::: badges
[R]{.badge} [Regression]{.badge} [Predictive Modeling]{.badge}
:::

Built a multiple linear regression model to predict life expectancy using socioeconomic and health indicators.

**Key Result**

The final model achieved an adjusted R² of approximately 0.98.

Adult mortality and HIV incidence emerged as major predictors.

### Explainable Machine Learning for Malaria Risk

**Malaria Among Pregnant Women in Ghana**

::: badges
[Machine Learning]{.badge} [KNN]{.badge} [Public Health]{.badge}
:::

Applied machine learning methods to Demographic and Health Survey data to predict malaria risk among pregnant women.

**Key Result**

The K-Nearest Neighbor model achieved the strongest performance with an AUC of approximately 0.88.
